The Telegraph (Melissa Lawford) — published 2026-09-29T05:34:00Z, confirmed from article metadata and URL path /2026/09/29/. Search highlights. NOTE: written BEFORE the speech (pre-speech analysis).
"Even the Right is turning against the triple lock"
ROBERT JENRICK, Reform UK Treasury spokesman, to The Telegraph: his party's commitment to the triple lock is "absolute and will not change". "We alone can afford it because we'll make more than £80bn a year in savings from the benefits bill, net zero, deporting low-skilled migrants and scrapping foreign aid."
Kemi Badenoch publicly defended the policy on Good Morning Britain this month.
The piece reports (single-sourced, anonymous) that a growing cohort in Tory and Reform circles accepts the triple lock commitment is looking untenable as Britain's debt pile surpasses £3tn; a senior Tory MP told a Westminster event this month the Conservatives should be the first party to ditch the triple lock and needed to "slaughter some sacred cows".
Notes the national care service could cost up to £18bn.
